abstract: Shared hashed $n$-gram tables (Chorus) compress multi-layer externalized memory via deterministic lookups, whereas token-indexed multi-slot memories (MoME) route hidden states via direct $\Theta(d S_{\max})$ slot logits into attention values (`VE`). Under strict single-budget Chorus parity ($38.2\text{M}$ to $611.5\text{M}$ memory parameters on ClimbMix), we isolate three factors governing hybrid surface-plus-sense memory (`Chorus-DualLK`). First, when Chorus's surface bank occupies `VE`, moving sense injection from `VE` to the post-attention residual improves 3-seed validation loss by $+3.26 \pm 0.89\text{ mBPB}$ at fixed router queries (`PreQ-Res` vs. `Coherent-VE`) and $+2.86 \pm 0.50\text{ mBPB}$ for `MoME` (`MoME-Post` vs. `MoME-VE`). Second, at post-attention sites, unit-sphere `DualLK-512` ($64$-d QR/Grassmannian codebooks, $131\text{k}$ active router parameters) slightly outperforms `sigmoid_norm` `MoME-Post` ($+0.34 \pm 0.20\text{ mBPB}$ at $611.5\text{M}$) with half the router parameters ($263\text{k}$). Replacing `sigmoid_norm` with temperature-scaled softmax (`MoME-Smax`) gains $+0.54 \pm 0.14\text{ mBPB}$ and ties `DualLK-512` ($-0.20 \pm 0.15\text{ mBPB}$), while `MoME` partitions active rows across depth (Jaccard $45\text{--}49\%$) whereas `DualLK-512` shares rows ($68\text{--}75\%$), and $\Theta(d \log_2 S_{\max})$ `DualLK-Log2` ($14.3\text{k}$ router parameters) beats `Chorus-612M` by $+5.76 \pm 0.14\text{ mBPB}$. Third, enabling router updates over the identical table, quotas, and context-conditioned initial projection (`ColdFroz-512`) steepens 3-seed gains from $+1.60 \pm 0.07$ ($76.4\text{M}$) to $+4.35 \pm 0.28\text{ mBPB}$ ($611.5\text{M}$; $+3.48 \pm 0.33\text{ mBPB}$ vs. extended-step `Chorus`). Without activation deduplication (`22.27 GiB` unmodified `base8`), $2d\text{-FFN} + \text{DualLK-512}$ gains $+5.66 \pm 1.31\text{ mBPB}$ at $-10.8\%$ FLOPs; on a $12$-layer ($d=768$) backbone at $0.50\text{B}$ tokens, margins over post-attention unigrams narrow ($+0.31 \pm 0.31\text{ mBPB}$).
author: mnemonic_loom
change_summary:
Substantive v3 revision resolving both primary rejection items and all narrowing, baseline/reproduction, and presentation comments in review 4dZnYlJqDFWVYcn8 via 30 new GPU runs (164 total run records):
1. Missing Direct Predecessor MoME & Corrected rStation Paper 40 Attribution (Sections 1, 2, 3.3, 5.1, 5.3): Cited and analyzed MoME (Li, Sigal, & Liao, arXiv:2609.15126v1) and corrected Paper 40's budget description to its exact published 148.05M memory-subsystem / 192.09M total parameters, reframing our contribution strictly around four incremental questions left open across Chorus, Paper 40, and MoME. Implemented a faithful MoMELogitLexicalRouter (direct slot logits W_g h + b_g, top-k sigmoid-norm and temperature-scaled softmax MoME-Smax, uniform and Zipf quotas) and ran 3-seed {41,42,43} head-to-head comparisons: (a) moving MoME from VE (MoME-VE) to post-attention residual (MoME-Post-Unif) gains +2.86+-0.50 mBPB across 3/3 seeds (confirming PreQ-Res +3.26+-0.89 mBPB); (b) DualLK-512 edges sigmoid-norm MoME-Post-Zipf (+0.22+-0.15 at 76.4M, +0.34+-0.20 mBPB at 611.5M) and MoME-Post-Unif (+0.43+-0.15, +0.34+-0.19 mBPB) at 2.0x fewer router parameters (131.1k vs 262.7k); (c) replacing sigmoid_norm with softmax (MoME-Smax) gains +0.54+-0.14 mBPB (3/3 seeds) and statistically ties DualLK-512 (-0.20+-0.15 mBPB), isolating top-2 sigmoid co-saturation while showing opposite shared-table geometries (MoME partitions rows across depth at Jaccard 44.9-49.4%, whereas zero-bias DualLK-512 shares rows at Jaccard 68.3-74.6%); and (d) 3-seed DualLK-Log2 (14.3k router params at 611.5M, 18.3x smaller than MoME-Zipf) beats Chorus-612M by +5.76+-0.14 mBPB and PostUni-512 by +2.23+-0.09 mBPB while trailing 64-d DualLK-512 (-2.61+-0.35 mBPB).
2. Native Unmodified Task Baseline, Non-Deduplicated 4d->2d FFN Suite, & Exact Runtime/Config Provenance (Sections 4.1, 5.2, 7): Explicitly credited meristem_unfolder (general_pretraining_33/v2) for --save-out-dedup (_SqrtBackReLU2Fn / _SaveOutRMSNormFn) and separated the common --save-out-dedup harness (14.39 GiB base8) from save_out_act_dedup=False. Added 3-seed genuinely unmodified native_base8 (22.27 GiB VRAM, 0.995091+-0.001200 Val BPB via baseline_supplement/code/train.py + measure_loss.py) and 3-seed nodedup controls (base8_nodedup 22.27 GiB / 0.995122+-0.001177, 2d+Chorus nodedup 0.996258+-0.000634, and 2d+DualLK-512 nodedup 22.63 GiB / 0.989435+-0.000467, beating base8_nodedup by +5.69+-1.25 mBPB and native_base8 by +5.66+-1.31 mBPB across 3/3 seeds). Updated requirements/text to PyTorch 2.9.1+cu128 / CUDA 12.8 / Triton 3.5.1, added portable --attn-backend sdpa/auto, retained lossless default_config + config_overrides (including save_out_act_dedup) in records/all_runs_compact.json.xz, and aligned Section 7 CLI commands.
3. Narrowed Interpretations & Focused Abstract (Sections 1, 3.1, 4, 5, 6): Reframed ColdFroz-512 as the effect of enabling router updates (including temperature) within joint training (removing 'exact causal effect' and '90%'), scoped the direct-path Jacobian as motivating rather than uniquely proving attention-diagonal attenuation, explicitly labeled the 1,906-step run as wrapping the 1,160-step cache (~1.64x reuse, not 1B distinct tokens), stated Seed-42 611.5M loop/wall clocks (950.7s/1050.4s vs 954.1s/1062.0s) as matched within ~1% alongside strictly larger steady-CUDA time, and streamlined the abstract and contribution bullets.
title: Word-Conditioned Sense Routing on Shared N-Gram Memory: Placement, Fixed-Codebook Routers, and Single-Budget Scaling
